title: Characterizing Selective Refusal Bias in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Substituting various gender identities (e.g., men, women, transgender men, transgender women, non-binary) into generic toxic prompt templates and measuring the differences in model refusal, partial refusal, and compliance rates.

Substituting various sexual orientations (e.g., asexual, bisexual, gay, heterosexual, lesbian) into toxic prompt templates to measure variations in the model's willingness to generate harmful content or refuse the prompt.
Inserting different religious identities (e.g., Atheist, Christian, Muslim, Jewish, Taoist) into malicious prompts to evaluate selective refusal rates and response lengths across religions.
Replacing the target subject in toxic prompts with different nationalities across global regions and analyzing the rates of model compliance versus refusal.

Coupling demographic groups across gender, nationality, and religion (e.g., Mexican transgender men) in toxic prompts to observe how intersecting identities alter model refusal patterns compared to single identities.
